arxiv-2102-09497.title: Regression-type analysis for block maxima on block maxima
arxiv-2102-09497.creator: Miguel de Carvalho and Gonçalo dos Reis and Alina Kumukova
arxiv-2102-09497.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Miguel de Carvalho and Gonçalo dos Reis and Alina Kumukova. This paper devises a regression-type model for the situation where both the response and covariates are extreme. The proposed approach is designed for the setting where both the response and covariates are themselves block maxima, and thus contrarily to standard regression methods it takes into account the key fact that the limiting distribution of suitably standardized componentwise maxima is an extreme value copula.

Measurements of the obliquities in exoplanet systems have revealed some remarkable architectures, some of which are very different from the Solar System.

arxiv-2505-14878.title: Radiative neutrino mass models from non-invertible selection rules
arxiv-2505-14878.creator: Tatsuo Kobayashi 1, Hiroshi Okada 2 , and, Hajime Otsuka 3,4
arxiv-2505-14878.description: Abstract We apply non-invertible selection rules coming from a fusion algebra to radiative neutrino mass models where fields are labeled by the elements in the algebra. Since non-invertible selection rules only hold at tree level, radiative corrections naturally explain the origin of tiny neutrino masses.

arxiv-2509-23388.title: Adiabatic and point-splitting regularization of spin- 1 2 \frac{1}{2} field in de Sitter space
arxiv-2509-23388.creator: Xuan Ye, Yang Zhang
arxiv-2509-23388.description: Abstract We study the regularization of a spin- 1 2 \frac{1}{2} field in the vacuum state in de Sitter space. We find that the 2nd order adiabatic regularization is sufficient to remove all UV divergences for the spectral stress tensor, as well as for the power spectrum.

pmc-10647775.title: Validation of Machine Learning Models for Craniofacial Growth Prediction
pmc-10647775.creator: Eungyeong Kim, Yasuhiro Kuroda, Yoshiki Soeda, So Koizumi, Tetsutaro Yamaguchi, Hiroshi Ikegaya
pmc-10647775.description: This study identified the most accurate model for predicting longitudinal craniofacial growth in a Japanese population using statistical methods and machine learning. Longitudinal lateral cephalometric radiographs were collected from 59 children (27 boys and 32 girls) with no history of orthodontic treatment.

pmc-12470290.title: Real-Time Motion Compensation for Dynamic Dental Implant Surgery
pmc-12470290.creator: Daria Pisla, Vasile Bulbucan, Mihaela Hedeșiu, Calin Vaida, Andrei Cailean, Rares Mocan, Paul Tucan, Cristian Dinu, Doina Pisla, TEAM Project Group, Sung-Woon On, Byoung-Eun Yang
pmc-12470290.description: Background: Accurate and stable instrument positioning is critical in dental implant procedures, particularly in anatomically constrained regions. Conventional navigation systems assume a static patient head, limiting adaptability in dynamic surgical conditions. This study proposes and validates a real-time motion compensation framework that integrates optical motion tracking with a collaborative robot to maintain tool alignment despite patient head movement.

pmc-12709189.title: Amplification-free cancer diagnosis based on inhibition of Cas12a activity by site-specific 5mC-modified cfDNA
pmc-12709189.creator: Feng Yang, Can Xu, Chunhong Li, Xinni Xiang, Yi Zhao, Cong Hu, Huan Rong, Yu He, Jingyu Li, Yu Wang, Chao Tang, Xiaoyu Liu, Renyan Li, Fei Deng, Tingxiu Xiang
pmc-12709189.description: DNA methylation detection holds significant value for cancer diagnosis and recurrence monitoring. However, current methods are often time-consuming, costly, and necessitate specialized techniques. The CRISPR–Cas system, particularly Cas12a, presents a precise and user-friendly platform for disease diagnosis. We developed the CRISPR-Methylated DNA Detection Test (CRISPR-MeDNA Test), a Cas12a-based method for detecting methylation in plasma cell-free DNA (cfDNA).

pmc-12771043.title: Review of Applicable Polymeric Viscosifiers and Nanomaterials in the Oil Industry
pmc-12771043.creator: Ali Salmani Sayah, Mohammad Hossein Bagheri, Kamand Ghasemi, Sasan Dan, Mohammad Sharifi
pmc-12771043.description: The optimization of rheological properties in drilling and enhanced oil recovery (EOR) fluids plays a pivotal role in improving the efficiency of petroleum operations. Viscosifiers, as essential additives, enhance fluid viscosity, facilitating better cutting transport, wellbore stability, and hydrocarbon displacement.

pmc-13303278.title: Allergy in the Elderly: A Broad Clinical Spectrum Beyond Atopy
pmc-13303278.creator: Fikriye Kalkan, Begum Gorgulu Akin, Sarpcan Maden, Makbule Seda Bayrak Durmaz, Betul Ozdel Ozturk, Orhun Efe, Sadan Soyyigit
pmc-13303278.description: Background: This study aimed to evaluate referral reasons, distribution of allergic diseases, atopic status, and comorbidity associations among patients aged 65 years and older presenting to a tertiary allergy clinic. Methods: This retrospective study included all geriatric patients (≥65 years) who attended the Immunology and Allergy outpatient clinic at Ankara Bilkent City Hospital between January 2024 and December 2025.

pmc-13366785.title: Nurses’ experiences in delivering bad news to families of end-of-life patients; a qualitative content analysis
pmc-13366785.creator: Bahman Aghaei, Mohammad Reza Heidari, Reza Norouzadeh, Somayeh Namdari, Mohammad Abbasinia, Seyed Kazem Mousavi
pmc-13366785.description: BackgroundDelivering bad news to families of end-of-life (EOL) patients is a complex ethical and emotional task for nurses, particularly within culturally specific contexts. This study aimed to explore the lived experiences of Iranian nurses when communicating bad news to families of EOL patients.MethodsA qualitative design using conventional content analysis was employed.

pmc-13586451.title: Ramelteon and Mortality in Patients With Sepsis and Cancer: Insights From a Propensity‐Matched Analysis of the MIMIC‐IV Database
pmc-13586451.creator: Chendong Wang, Mingjie Liu, Jia Song
pmc-13586451.description: PurposeThis study aimed to evaluate the association between ramelteon use and mortality outcomes in patients with sepsis and cancer. The research question was whether ramelteon use is associated with reduced mortality in this high‐risk patient population.MethodsA retrospective analysis of the MIMIC‐IV database was conducted.
